title: Patenting Quantum Computing Innovations – Part 5: Shor’s Algorithm and Conclusions - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Part 5 of a patent-law series (bylined in text by Sinan Utku of Covington & Burling) argues that a Shor's-algorithm RSA-decryption claim would likely be found patent-ineligible under the Mayo/Alice framework as an abstract mathematical method, despite USPTO guidance treating RSA encryption as eligible. It concludes that uncertain US patent-eligibility law is a barrier for quantum innovators and that reform via the pending Patent Eligibility Restoration Act faces Congressional paralysis.
